claims.body: The Avalanche are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Devils are one of the best at keeping shots away. Hot take: the Avalanche break through anyway.

claims.head: Who blinks first?
claims.body: The Devils are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Avalanche are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Devils’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.

claims.head: Top line on top line: Hughes against MacKinnon
claims.call: The Devils’ L1 (Gritsyuk, Hughes and Bratt) spends at least 38% of its 5-on-5 time against the Avalanche’s first line.
claims.body: At home, the Devils keep sending Hughes’s line (Gritsyuk, Hughes and Bratt) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Sheldon Keefe has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Avalanche’s first line is Lehkonen, MacKinnon and Nečas.

notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 5 of their last 9 games, including the last one. Fedor Svechkov takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Noah Juulsen is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Manson and Kulak.
Gavin Brindley was added to the roster on Oct 15 and has played beside Parker Kelly and Fedor Svechkov.
Zachary L'Heureux is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 36% with his old team last season.
Luke Evangelista is out (illness) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-six forward. Dawson Mercer has taken his spot beside Timo Meier and Nico Hischier.
Connor Brown has not played this season. He is a top-six forward. Arseny Gritsyuk has taken his spot beside Jesper Bratt and Jack Hughes.
Connor Brown is expected back after missing 8 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Johnathan Kovacevic was added to the roster on Oct 11 and has played beside Declan Chisholm.

NJD.head: Advantage, the Devils
NJD.body: Colorado is on the second night of a back-to-back, while New Jersey has home-ice advantage. Then again, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents lately, and New Jersey will be without Glass. The Avalanche can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

COL.head: A tough matchup for the Avalanche
COL.body: Colorado is on the second night of a back-to-back, while New Jersey has home-ice advantage. Then again, Colorado has been out-chancing opponents lately, and New Jersey will be without Glass. The Avalanche can pull it off if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: Something has to give
paras: The Avalanche come in at 5-3-1, the Devils at 4-4-0.

It’s strength against strength: the Avalanche are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Devils are one of the best at keeping shots away. At home, Sheldon Keefe likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Avs’ first line.

items.text: The Devils are newly without Luke Evangelista, and have had to make do without Connor Brown all season.
Brock Nelson has six goals in eight games against New Jersey since 2023-24, most of them with the Islanders.
Jack Hughes has scored in three straight games against Colorado.
Artturi Lehkonen has a point in four straight games.
